text: Event management with schedule validation and scheduler status.
Keep best-effort backup/restore on failed redefinition; wording and implementation become DBLoom's own.
Database-wide search with five match types.
Table search form with per-column operators.
Column find/replace with preview and regex mode.
Keep CHECK/ANALYZE/CHECKSUM/OPTIMIZE/REPAIR; drop DisableMultiTableMaintenance config key.
Row format per engine; drop PBXT, Barracuda/legacy InnoDB file format logic.
Keep AUTO_INCREMENT and engine options; gate by server/engine, not legacy detection.
Move/rename/copy table incl. cross-db.
Batch table prefix add/replace.
Keep multi-row insert form; row count default becomes DBLoom setting rather than $cfg.
Per-row UPDATE with unique WHERE and LIMIT 1.
Per-row delete with safe unique condition.
Unique-row condition from PK/unique key or full-row fallback.
Keep per-type value encoding; ProtectBinary becomes a DBLoom setting.
Inline edit and edit-next flow; no PHP session state, client/URL state instead.
Report insert id and affected rows, but compute ids correctly (legacy multi-row id adjustment is inexact).
Column transformation feature depends on config storage; decide once. (owner decision 2026-10-23, feature: column transformations)
Preview generated SQL without executing.
Keep paging/page size/full-partial text/relational display; state in client/user settings not PHP session or $cfg.
Keep click-to-sort with multi-column and smart direction; default order becomes a setting.
Create-table guards and column count cap of 4096.
Keep paged tree loading; page sizes become DBLoom settings, no DisableIS variants.
Keep prefix grouping of databases/tables; separators and depth become DBLoom settings.
Keep filter box, natural ordering, hidden items; thresholds become DBLoom settings.
Keep related-value dropdown/popup picker; limit and order become DBLoom settings.
Avoid redundant COUNT queries when page already shows full result.
Show the true query and true server error; do not apply automatic LIMIT to failing queries.
Signed GET SQL no longer needed if SQL is not passed in URLs; use server-side state and CSRF protection instead.
Keep a guard on DROP DATABASE via DBLoom permissions and mandatory confirmation, not a PHP config flag or client-supplied confirm field.
Row identification passed between views must be tamper-proof; use server-side state or signed row keys, not Core::signSqlQuery; fix silent discard.
Custom WHERE/ORDER power-user input stays but is validated or parsed; run under user's own privileges, parameterize where possible.
Enum, set and foreign-key value pickers remain useful in insert/edit/search forms.
Keep explicit confirmation for destructive actions; implement as UI dialog with server-side check, not localized "Yes" POST value.
Saved named export presets per user stored in DBLoom own app storage, not la_export_templates or Configuration Storage.
Keep sensible SQL export defaults; defaults live in settings design, not PHP cfg keys.
Keep sensible general export defaults; drop PHP ZipDump/GZipDump config; defaults set via DBLoom settings.
Keep sensible import option defaults; defaults set via DBLoom settings, not PHP cfg.
Offer SQL, CSV, JSON, XML and chosen others; drop CodeGen, PHP array, Texy, Word 2000; remaining formats are an owner scope choice via format registry.
Per-format choice of structure, data, or both remains; invalid values rejected rather than silently falling back.
Formats without text view are download-only; keep as format capability flag in registry.
Keep SQL dump options (DDL, drop, triggers, routines, FK disable, transaction); drop legacy compatibility modes for old servers and PHP version comment.
Configurable separator, enclosure, escape, line terminator, NULL string, header row remain.
Keep Excel-friendly CSV preset (separator, BOM/encoding); drop legacy Mac Excel 2003/2008 variants.
Pretty-print and unicode options remain; implemented via native JSON serialization.
Exporting result of a free-typed query remains; unsupported formats report a clear error; filename export.<ext>.
Server, database, table and query-result export scopes remain; invalid parameter combinations rejected with proper error.
Database export filters by selected tables; show message when none selected.
Forced structure/data override and optional table read lock with guaranteed unlock remain.
View export output in read-only viewer with copy; Back/Refresh POST replay is PHP form mechanics and dropped.
Keep zip and gzip output; availability no longer depends on PHP functions or cfg flags.
Compress-on-the-fly becomes native streaming gzip with bounded memory, not a PHP memory budget option.
Optional server-side save to configured directory remains if enabled; keep filename sanitization, overwrite guard, write errors; setting in 12-settings.
Compressed export gains .zip/.gz extension and matching MIME type; format extension appended when absent.
Keep multi-file zip export with one file per table; implement with Node archive library.
Keep filename templates with date and server/db/table/columns placeholders; drop PHP strftime and legacy aliases and LEGACYADMIN token.
Remember template per export scope in per-user settings stored in DBLoom storage, not pma user values.
Keep pasted SQL and uploaded file sources; bookmarks depend on owner bookmark decision; oversized upload message adapted, no FAQ reference.
Closed set of import formats stays as registry; final format list is owner scope choice; reject unknown formats.
Keep streaming statement-by-statement SQL import with skip-errors and skip-first-N; use own SQL splitter; resumable timeout handling not needed.
Delimiters, enclosure, escape, line ending, replace/ignore, partial import, header row, column list, new table/db creation remain.
Column type inference and CREATE TABLE plus INSERT generation for new-table import remains useful.
Keep LOAD DATA INFILE option with LOCAL capability probing; MySQL 8.4 has local_infile off by default, handle accordingly.
Browser upload plus optional server-side upload directory; keep path traversal and symlink protection; directory configured via settings.
Transparent gzip, bzip2 and zip import stays; no PHP extension or cfg gating; bzip2 optional.
Strip UTF-8 and UTF-16 byte-order marks on first chunk; may also use BOM for charset detection.
Convert file charset to UTF-8 on read using Node encoding libraries; SET NAMES fallback for missing iconv not needed.
Report failing statement with server error and abort unless ignore-errors set; transactional rollback only for transactional tables; no mysqlDie.
Disable FK checks during import and always restore, including on errors.
Keep success summary with count and filename; UI refresh after DDL via client state invalidation, not panel reload.
Progress feedback for long uploads stays, implemented with browser upload events or streaming, not PHP polling route.
Default format remembered per user in settings, overridable by URL parameter; no cfg array.
CSV options: header row, NULL text, separator, enclosure, escape, line terminator, CRLF removal; drop PHP_EOL detail.
Excel-compatible CSV variant stays (separator, CRLF, BOM-aware); drop Mac Excel 2003/2008 editions.
Correct value formatting for NULL, numeric, binary hex, BIT, geometry, strings; INSERT/REPLACE/UPDATE statement types.
JSON export stays; header should name DBLoom and version; binary and geometry handling kept.
Skip tables larger than a given size on database export.
Separate-files ZIP stays with sane entry naming; drop first-dot extension quirk.
Filename template with db/table/date tokens stays; replace strftime and legacyadmin tokens with safe own token set.
Server, database and table scope export with selection of databases, tables, structure/data; views after tables.
Parse CSV with configurable terminator, enclosure, escape, line end, with parameter validation; shown inline not mysqlDie.
LOAD DATA import optional, table scope; escape all interpolated values; refuse compressed input unless decompressed first.
Clear upload error messages stay for size, partial, missing file; no php.ini references.
Dry-run affected row count for single-table UPDATE/DELETE.
SQL editor runs queries via its own API, not an import route; keep bookmark/parameter support per other decisions.
Long buffered exports need keepalive or streaming to avoid proxy timeouts; use streaming instead of X-pmaPing.
Import must stream in chunks with bounded memory; chunk sizes are implementation choice.
Resumable large imports stay as need; use job-based import with offset, not resubmitting the file.
Configurable max upload size shown in UI, enforced server-side; not php.ini based.
Sanitize download filenames against traversal and header injection; drop url_rewriter.
Do not interpolate unescaped LDI terminators, charset names or USE detection; validate or quote all.
Quick versus Custom export modes stay; preference stored in user settings.
Format dropdown with option panel per selected format.
Single-table export row range selection with record count and LIMIT.
